name: Central bank stress
value: Fed, ECB, BoJ eye December rises; BoE 4%
summary: Fed, ECB and BoJ all leaning to December rate rises as inflation climbs; BoE raised to 4% on 5 Nov
state: October US CPI, released on 10 Nov, firmed expectations of a Fed rate rise at its 8–9 Dec meeting (Yahoo Finance). Markets priced about a 66% chance of an ECB rise in December, with Lagarde due to step down early (Trading Economics, 9 Nov), and a BoJ summary on 10 Nov pointed to a December rise (Japan Times). The Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov. Policymakers face rising inflation and slowing growth; no emergency move was found.
for_you: Rising interest rates push up mortgage, loan and credit card costs and lift savings rates. Bank of England decisions set UK borrowing costs.
rubric_hit: Stagflationary dilemma across major central banks (Watch); no emergency or inter-meeting moves

sources.title: Yahoo Finance — October CPI inflation comes in hotter than expected
The Japan Times — BOJ summary suggests good chance of December interest rate hike
Trading Economics — France 10-year bond yield news

why: Central banks are the shock absorbers; when they are boxed in or their independence is challenged, markets lose their backstop.
drivers: Inflation vs growth trade-off, political pressure, currency moves, financial stability.

rubric.alert: Emergency inter-meeting moves, attempt to remove a central-bank head, or coordinated intervention.
rubric.watch: Stagflationary dilemma, open political pressure on a major central bank, or FX intervention by a G7 bank.
rubric.normal: Fed, ECB and BoJ acting orderly and on schedule; independence unquestioned.
